chapter: Opinions on pop music, jazz education and the business
title: Berklee, Harvard and the teaching of jazz roots
summary: Wilson and Ted Jr. discuss Berklee's size and cost, jazz at Harvard, and Ted Jr.'s loss of his Kingsborough job.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Well, Berklee has got a great start, if

they would just improve the curriculum. Because they've got people from 60 countries of the world up there, they've got 2600 students, and there are a lot of people studying up there, aren't they? And they are in the most favored position to have that, just the best courses.
It's nice to hear that.
Because they do have it -- and they charge plenty of money, too, and they get it.
That's good to hear.
They're more expensive than a lot of other schools, I tell you.

And you'd have to insist in these schools -- perhaps we could get someone on the National Foundation of the Arts or someone that can stress this sort of thing, that this is what academically is needed.
Now there's a jazz course in Harvard. Maybe they do that there, in Eastman and these other schools, they may be already teaching what you were talking about, Ted.
But do they do it in that kind of detail?
Well, Tom Everett told me he's teaching at Harvard what you do.
Yeah?
Yeah. Because I was telling him
about what you do. I was telling him about you teaching out there, but now he's doing it himself.
That's in a City University. Maybe elsewhere ...

Well, yeah. See, out here, they got their own little radio stations, these schools out here have their own stations where they play jazz and blues and their version of pop and folk. The student programs run the radio stations.

But they make a point of people knowing about the funeral bands in New Orleans and the early days of Joe King Oliver and all those things that led to Chicago. They don't just say, well, that existed, and then jump right to the ..
New York is so spread around, though, with the ethnic groups.
Well, your work is really cut out for you to do, Teddy.
Well, I can't fight an administrator -- that's what I lost in 1977.
Well, maybe Kingsboro that area out there on Oriental Blvd. in Brooklyn is the wrong place for jazz. Maybe in Harlem or Manhattan, that would be better.
Your dad just said you can't kill us all; you can't make us stop. So don't you think that ...
